summary: Babylon.js is an open-source web rendering engine and application framework from Microsoft and community contributors, shipping as one core package plus official sibling packages for asset loading, asset saving, user interface, add-ons and editors; the newest release when this was written is 9.22.1, published 2026-08-20. It is far more than a renderer: it covers the scene graph, animation, skinning, morph targets, instancing, glTF import and export with a very wide extension set, Gaussian splat rendering, a node-based material system, a node-based frame graph, and a full immersive session stack on the WebXR Device API with controller, hand, eye and body tracking. Physics is not in the engine at all. Every physics row below is delivered by a plug-in wrapping an outside engine: Havok is the only one on the current second-generation physics interface, and Ammo.js on the older interface is the only one that does soft bodies and cloth. It does no networking, no shared state, no identity and no persistence beyond writing a file on the client, so a multi-user world built on it must get all of that from somewhere else. Three traps for a standards audience: the scene is left-handed and Y-up by default, so right-handed glTF content is imported under a wrapper node carrying a negative Z scale unless the application opts into a right-handed scene; the WebGPU engine, which the project itself calls complete, still has no multiview, so immersive sessions in practice run on WebGL; and the loaders reach out to Babylon's own content network by default to fetch the Draco, meshopt, KTX2 and Basis decoders, which the project's own documentation warns against in production. Levels below read 'native' for anything shipped and maintained by the Babylon.js project itself, with the package named in the note, and 'via-extension' for anything that needs software from outside the project.
